Apps can access and [define a user's master list of categories](/en-us/graph/api/outlookuser-post-mastercategories).
Additionally, app users can change the importance of a message (or event or task), or flag a message for follow-up.
Apps can set up [Inbox rules](/en-us/graph/api/resources/messagerule) to promptly handle incoming messages and reduce email clutter.
Mail tips can alert apps of certain conditions so to take more efficient follow-up actions instead.
The people API can suggest persons most relevant to a user, based on the user’s communication and collaboration patterns and business relationships.

**Rich notifications**: Change notifications that include the resource data of the object that changed.

One user who found Outlook opening links in Edge switched it back to the default browser and said it took all of 60 seconds to google the answer.

Opening Outlook links in Edge has some upside because Edge keeps you logged into 365, so company links and attachments open more easily. The user wished it were smarter, though: for people working across multiple orgs, it should open the link under the 365 profile matching the mailbox being read.

A paying Microsoft customer noticed Outlook's link handling on a personal machine and figured out how to turn it off, but called it very annoying: "I'm not going to be annoyed into using edge - I won't be tricked into it either."
"It took us half a day to roll back our systems to get rid of the new Outlook. It's a web based email client through an Edge browser window and it's awful."
Counterpoint from another user: "The web based outlook is an extremely well-polished and usable piece of software. You can use it in any browser you like."
A user reports Outlook has been opening mailto links in the Windows Mail app, which they have never once used, so Outlook is overriding their defaults there too.

New Outlook compared with Fastmail's web client, which is as fast as or faster than Outlook Classic: "The new Outlook is just bad. Load order is wrong, it renders everything on every window, loads unnecessary data, etc."
"Anytime a relative installs a new machine I get the call 'What is wrong with outlook?'. It's always 'new'."
After switching networks or SSIDs, Outlook refuses to respond or come into focus until it finishes some kind of synchronization, even when the user just wants to look at an already-open email.

The free Outlook that replaced Windows Mail was so bad that it made one user finally switch to Thunderbird. They sometimes miss the Copilot integration, but say copy-pasting into Thunderbird is still faster than using Copilot in Outlook.
Biggest issue with new Outlook on Windows is meeting reminders: a loading screen with the Outlook logo shows for about 5 seconds before the meeting name and dismiss button appear.
Outlook for Mac is surprisingly good: "Every interaction feels (and is) native." The user credited the team behind it.
One user finds it faster to search their email through an LLM with an MCP/cloud integration than to use Outlook's search field in the browser.
The Outlook web app breaks browser navigation, but it loads almost instantly (under a second).
"'Old' Outlook is slow enough as well. Especially with Corporate 'security' software."
"After 20+ years on Outlook, I recently switched to Thunderbird. Not quite as full featured and a little slow at times, but it's finally a viable replacement for Outlook."

For email-only users, Claws Mail is recommended as lightning fast compared to Outlook and stable. Outlook .pst mail and contacts can be converted to mbox with the readpst utility (libpst) and imported.

Users report the ad and advertising-preferences issue only affects free accounts. M365 Personal/Family and paid business or corporate Office 365 accounts don't show an Advertising section or those popups.
A user's wife complained her "email changed" when it became Outlook with ads. He said: "damn it I pay for email not to have this s*t" and is considering moving her to Thunderbird.
A user with multiple Gmail and Outlook accounts says the official Windows clients are very slow, especially Outlook, which stops responding for about half a minute when opening.
